lines.text: What does going to school cost?
Education at the primary school and secondary school is free.
But there are costs:
Childcare under the age of four: the costs differ per municipality or daycare centre and are often dependent on your income.
After-school care [buitenschoolse opvang], from age four, you must pay for yourself; sometimes you also pay for care during the lunch break.
The parental contribution [ouderbijdrage]: the school asks parents to pay something for, for example, a school trip or celebrations.
The amount differs per school, but the ouderbijdrage is voluntary [vrijwillig].
Learning materials [lesmateriaal]: you do not have to pay for books.
In secondary education there are sometimes costs for extra materials, for example a laptop or gym clothes [gymkleding] — not mandatory.
Travel costs [reiskosten]: if the school is further away, you pay for public transport [openbaar vervoer, OV] yourself.
School fees [schoolgeld]: until age eighteen, education is free.
Are you older than eighteen?
Then you pay tuition at the mbo [lesgeld] or tuition at the hbo or wo [collegegeld].
Private education [particulier onderwijs]: private schools are usually expensive; parents pay the costs to the school.
Child benefit and childcare allowance.
For all children under eighteen, parents receive child benefit [kinderbijslag]: money from the government [overheid], not dependent on income.
You must apply for it yourself at the SVB (Sociale Verzekeringsbank).
In addition, you can get childcare allowance [kinderopvangtoeslag] for childcare: money you get back from the tax office [Belastingdienst] — this one is dependent on income.
If you cannot pay for school.
You can talk with the school: request to pay less or nothing — your child can then still take part in everything.
You can get money back or borrow [lenen] from DUO (Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs), a government organisation; adults who continue studying can do this themselves.
The municipality can help, and so can Stichting Leergeld, for example with a bicycle or laptop for a child.

For refugees with an official residence permit, the civic integration course [inburgeringscursus] is free; others can borrow money for the inburgeringscursus from DUO (DUO determines whether your income is low enough).
The UAF helps refugees who want to study — including refugees who do not yet have an official residence permit — with information and sometimes with money.
